title: Ephemeral RBAC template generator with drift-aware health checks and least-privilege defaults
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that scaffolds IAM/RBAC role and policy artifacts for Private (VPC) deployments. Module should emit least-privilege role templates, support timebound/ephemeral roles, attach structured audit metadata, and expose drift-aware health checks for operator dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published under modules/priv_iam_role_factory with documented inputs/outputs
Module supports role templates (service, human, cross-account) with declarative permission slices
Timebound roles: TTL/expiry metadata applied and example workflow for ephemeral creds included
Policy sanitizer: linter step that rejects broad actions (e.g. '*' on s3) unless explicit justification label provided
Automated drift check: small lambda or cloud function + scheduled run that compares desired policy document to live, emits metrics to Console
Unit integration tests (terratest) for three example stacks and CI job added
Design and security review complete and documented in Confluence (link provided)
tasks: Spike: survey existing internal IAM modules and list overlapping capabilities (complete)
Design: propose module input model and output shape, YAML-based role templates for readability
Implement: role templater + policy builder + optional managed policy attach
Health checks: implement drift detector and CloudWatch metric emitter
Testing: Terratest suites + CI pipeline integration
Docs: Confluence design page, module README with examples and migration guide
Security review: gather SRE/InfoSec signoff and add remediation flows

notes: Design trade-offs: we weighed two approaches for ephemeral roles — short-lived session tokens (STS) vs ephemeral role resources that are created/destroyed. Chosen approach: short-lived sessions (STS) combined with TTL tag and a housekeeping job to revoke long-running sessions. This reduces IAM churn and Terraform state churn.

Policy model: adopt 'permission-slices' where a role is constructed from narrow slices (read-only-s3, write-logs, kms-decrypt) to encourage composition and code reuse. Default slices are conservative; customers can opt-in to expanded slices with a documented risk justification.

Upgrade path: provide a migration script that maps old role names (from iam-role-factory) to new templated roles; include a safe rollback plan and CI job to verify no active sessions are broken during migration.

Rollout plan: stage in three phases - (1) internal infra teams in staging, (2) select customers under a feature flag in Dedicated, (3) general availability. Console feature will expose health metrics and a one-click remediation for simple policy drift fixes.

Open questions: how to surface expired role telemetry in existing Console traces vs adding a new index. Security prefers adding a tag-based index; Ops prefers minimal telemetry changes to avoid increased ingestion costs. Follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-20.
